transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I'll start talking about my overnight shift at work, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or... paint colors, or patient charts. I can just see everyone getting lost while I'm talking to them, and I don't really know how to fix it.

Over the past week or two, have you noticed that your mood has been unusually elevated or that you have a lot more energy than normal, like you need less sleep or feel like you can do many things at once?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. Honestly, I've just been feeling... really down and drained. I definitely don't have extra energy, and I'm not doing a bunch of things at once. I just feel pretty exhausted most of the time.
Have you been experiencing any beliefs that feel very real to you but that others don't seem to share, or have you heard voices or seen things that others around you don't seem to notice?

Well, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. But... I do know that my supervisors are watching me. I'm sure they changed my shifts on purpose, and I know they watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm, like, unsafe or doing something wrong. People at work keep telling me it's just because of staffing shortages, but I know that's not true. I can tell they're watching me.

When did you first start noticing that your supervisors were watching you and that your shifts were being changed on purpose? Did this start before you began feeling down and exhausted, or did it come after you started feeling that way?

I think the whole camera thing started first. I mean, there was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't feeling so down and exhausted... I wasn't in that deep depressed place yet. But I still knew the supervisors were monitoring me. I kept acting really guarded at work because of it. So yeah, I was already dealing with them watching me before the exhaustion and the low mood really hit.
Right now, today, do you still believe that your supervisors are watching you through the cameras and changing your shifts on purpose, even though you're feeling down and exhausted?

Yeah, I still know they're doing it. Actually, it seems like... when this low mood is at its absolute worst, that's when I'm the most convinced that they're watching me through the cameras. It gets so intense that my speech gets all tangled up. I just can't even explain myself clearly when it happens, but I know they're watching.

When you think back to those few weeks before you started feeling really down and exhausted, how convinced were you at that time that the supervisors were watching you? Were you as certain about it then as you are now, or has your certainty about it grown stronger as your mood got worse?

I was definitely sure about it back then, too. I mean, I knew they were watching me even before I started feeling so tired and low. But... I guess you could say it feels stronger now. Like, when the depression is really bad, the feeling that they're monitoring me just kind of takes over everything. So, yeah, I was certain then, but it's definitely gotten more intense as my mood got worse.

When you think back to those few weeks before the exhaustion and low mood started, did you have any concerns about your safety or your job performance at work, or was the belief about the cameras and monitoring completely separate from any worries like that?

I didn't really have any worries about my job performance or anything like that. I mean, I do my job fine. It was just... I just knew they were watching me. It didn't have anything to do with me being worried about getting fired or messing up. It was just a fact that the cameras were on me and they were doing it on purpose.

Going back further—before those few weeks when you first noticed the camera monitoring, was there a longer period of time when you felt completely normal, with no worries about being watched and no depression either?

Well, no, not really. I mean, this whole thing... it's been going on for a while now. About a year and five months, I think. It all started right after they changed my schedule at work. I used to have just steady day shifts, but then they switched me to rotating nights and started throwing in all this overtime. That's when everything started. So, no, there hasn't been a time recently where I felt completely normal before all this.

Let me make sure I have the timeline right. You said the camera monitoring started about 1 year and 5 months ago when your work schedule changed. At that exact time when your schedule first changed and you first started noticing the cameras—were you already feeling down and exhausted then, or did the low mood and exhaustion come later?

No, the low mood came a little bit later. The camera stuff started right when they changed my schedule, about a year and five months ago. But I didn't start feeling really down and exhausted until... well, I guess the depression and just losing interest in everything has been with me for about a year and two months. So there was a gap there at the beginning where it was just the cameras before the depression hit.

During those first few weeks when you first noticed the cameras watching you—before the depression started—did you have any depressed mood at all during that time, or were you feeling emotionally okay?

No, I wasn't feeling down then. There was a stretch of a few weeks right at the start where I wasn't in that deep depressed place at all. Emotionally, I guess I was fine. But I still absolutely believed the cameras and the supervisors were monitoring me, so... I just kept acting really guarded at work. The depression part didn't happen until a bit later.

During those first few weeks when you noticed the cameras and believed the supervisors were monitoring you—before the depression started—did you experience any other unusual beliefs or strange perceptions? For example, did you feel like things around you had special hidden meanings meant for you, or did you notice any other odd things happening that seemed directed at you?

No, not really. I mean, I didn't think there were hidden messages or anything like that. It was just the cameras and knowing the supervisors were watching me. That was the only thing going on. I didn't notice anything else strange happening.

In those first few weeks when you started noticing the cameras—before your depression began—did you feel suspicious or paranoid about other things in your life, or was the belief about your supervisors watching you pretty much the only concerning thing you were focused on?

No, it was just the supervisors and the cameras. I wasn't... I wasn't paranoid about anything else. I didn't think anyone else was following me or anything. It was strictly just about work and them keeping tabs on me there. Everything else in my life seemed fine at that point.

During those first few weeks when you first started believing the supervisors were watching you through the cameras—before the depression started—did you ever feel confused about what was real, or did you have any trouble distinguishing your thoughts from reality?

No, I wasn't confused about what was real. I mean... to me, the cameras were real. I didn't feel like my mind was playing tricks on me or anything like that. I knew what my own thoughts were, and I just knew they were watching me. I didn't have any trouble telling the difference between my thoughts and what was going on around me.

During those first few weeks when you started noticing the camera monitoring—before the depression began—were you able to work normally and get through your shifts without any problems, or did you notice that your ability to do your job or focus at work was changing in any way?

Well, at first I thought I was working normally, but... it definitely started affecting things. I started needing my coworkers to double-check my rounds and my charting because I just couldn't focus. And it wasn't just at work. At home, I've fallen behind on my bills, I've completely ignored my friends, and my apartment is just... it's out of control. It actually got bad enough at work that employee health sent me for an emergency evaluation. That was after I admitted I was having thoughts about suicide. So, yeah, it definitely changed how I was functioning.

During those first few weeks when you started noticing the cameras being watching you—before the depression began—did you notice that your speech was becoming jumbled or hard to follow, the way it is now? Or was your thinking and speaking clear back then?

No, back then it was pretty clear. I could talk normally. But now... that's actually a big part of why I'm here. I just can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. I'll start trying to tell someone about my overnight shift, and then somehow I'm jumping to talking about soccer, and then paint colors, and then back to patient charts. I can literally see people getting lost while I'm talking to them. It wasn't like that at first, but it's really bad now.

During those first few weeks when you started noticing the cameras watching you—before the depression began—did you feel like you had more energy than usual, need less sleep, or feel like you could accomplish a lot of things at once? Or did your energy and sleep feel pretty normal back then?

No, I didn't feel anything like that. My energy was normal back then. I didn't feel like I could do a bunch of things at once, and I was sleeping the same as always. I didn't have extra energy or anything.

When you first started noticing the cameras watching you those few weeks before the depression began—during that time when you were feeling emotionally okay—did you have any other strange experiences or beliefs about yourself or the world around you that felt unusual, even if they weren't about being watched at work?

No, not really. I mean, it was just the cameras. I didn't have any other weird thoughts or, you know, strange experiences like that. Everything else seemed pretty normal to me at the time, besides the feeling of being monitored.

During those first few weeks when you started noticing the cameras watching you—before the depression began—did you notice any changes in how you were thinking or organizing your thoughts? For example, did your thoughts ever feel scattered, jump around, or feel hard to organize, even though your speech was still clear?

No, not back then. My thoughts felt pretty normal. I mean, I wasn't having trouble keeping things straight in my head or anything. Like I said, it's really only lately that everything feels so scattered. Back when I first noticed the cameras, my thinking was completely fine.
